findings.claim: The diff adds a new shared module, backend/app/services/mtime.py, that no touch point names; seven core write paths now import it.
findings.impact: None that a user can hit. The module is the single place where whole-second truncation is defined for I1/I2/I14. A reader of the touch-point list would not know that a change to this helper reaches the scanner, upload, create-file, copy, content write and link-rewrite paths at once.
findings.evidence: backend/app/services/mtime.py:8-17 (new). Imported at scanner.py:38, content_write.py:11, fileops.py:29, markdown_relations.py:23, upload.py:25 and routers/drives.py:60. It is absent from the spec's Touch points section.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (this is a comparison against the touch-point list)

bucket_proposal.reason: An unplanned place, not a broken invariant: the helper's behaviour (int(st_mtime) to naive UTC) matches SPEC-CORE-137 step 1.

findings.claim: frontend/src/components/search/SearchQueryHeader.tsx changes behaviour by adding "modified" to the ConditionMenu entries list, and it is not a touch point. The list names only ConditionMenu.tsx and SearchFilterChips.tsx for the menu.
findings.impact: This array is what places 「更新日」 between 「長さ」 and 「お気に入り」 in the first level the user sees. The R-5 layout touch point and the order rule depend on it, yet the plan does not name the file. A later edit that reorders or drops the entry would land in an unplanned file.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/search/SearchQueryHeader.tsx:272-281: entries ["tag","kind","folder",collection,"size","duration","modified","favorite"]. It is the only ConditionMenu caller (grep ConditionMenu in non-test src). Existing tests SearchQueryHeader.scope.test.tsx and SearchQueryHeader.sizeDuration.test.tsx had their expected first-level lists updated to include "Modified".

bucket_proposal.reason: An unplanned file. The behaviour matches the spec's menu rule and is covered by SearchQueryHeader.modified.test.tsx, so no invariant breaks.

findings.claim: Five e2e fixture files gain modified_at on FileItem literals, but the touch points name only searchMerge.ts and FolderTreePane.tsx as FileItem literals that gain the field.
findings.impact: None at runtime. These are build inputs of the component and EPUB e2e harnesses that the required FileItem.modified_at forces to change, so the plan undercounts the places the type change reaches.
findings.evidence: frontend/e2e-components/fixtures/clipsRow.tsx:53, justifiedHold.tsx:55, notesLibrary.tsx:46, videoCardByline.tsx:41 and frontend/e2e-epub/preview/app.tsx:48 each add `modified_at: null`. Cause: frontend/src/types/index.ts:66 makes `modified_at: string | null` required on FileItem.

bucket_proposal.reason: An unplanned but mechanical consequence of a planned type change.

findings.claim: The diff edits frontend and mcp-server tests, including expectations in existing tests, that the touch points do not cover. The list names only backend/tests/, the addon's tests/ and core-search-vocabulary.test.ts. One mock also gains a field its type does not have.
findings.impact: No user impact. A reader cannot tell from the plan that existing assertions moved: the first-level menu order in SearchQueryHeader.scope/sizeDuration, and the exact get_collection query in mcp-server smartCollections.test.ts, which now expects tz. These look adjusted to the new behaviour, not loosened. FileDetailFullScreen.smartCollection.test.tsx:399 adds `modified_at: null` to a Smart Folder mock, which suggests SmartFolder carries the field when it does not.
findings.evidence: frontend/src/components/search/__tests__/SearchQueryHeader.scope.test.tsx:118 and SearchQueryHeader.sizeDuration.test.tsx:84-96 add "Modified" to the expected order. mcp-server/src/__tests__/smartCollections.test.ts:288,326 add `tz: Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`. frontend/src/components/__tests__/FileDetailFullScreen.smartCollection.test.tsx:388-401: savedSmartFolder() returns a Smart Folder object with `modified_at: null`. About 70 other frontend test files add `modified_at: null` to FileItem literals.

bucket_proposal.reason: Unplanned test reach. No assertion is weakened, and the stray Smart Folder field reads wrong without breaking anything.

findings.claim: The intelligence addon's own frontend calls parseSearchQuery/filterFromParsed for the Ask scope and its count. The diff reaches it through searchQuery.ts, but it is not a touch point, and a modified: token there is consumed as an operator and then dropped from the scope.
findings.impact: A user who types `modified:<1y` into the Ask scope gets a scope (and a scope count) without the condition, silently. Before this change the token was free text and was dropped the same way, and size:/duration: are already dropped there, so the visible outcome is unchanged. The token now sets hasOperators and is a parsed operator that the scope never sends.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/frontend/Page.tsx:103-127: scopeStringFromRaw keeps only path/in/tag/type, and askScopeFromString builds {folders, collections, tags, kinds} from filterFromParsed(parseSearchQuery(raw), null) with no modified argument. addons/intelligence/frontend/AskFindHeader.tsx:54-61: the count listing sends folder/collection/tag/type only.
findings.repro: not_reproduced (read only). Predicted: Ask scope `path:Downloads modified:<1y` counts and scopes every file under Downloads.

bucket_proposal.reason: The Ask scope is outside SPEC-CORE-138 (the spec says MCP Ask sends no filter), and size:/duration: already behave this way. It is an unplanned consumer of the changed parser, not a broken invariant.

specification_compliance: Touch-point comparison: the diff reaches backend/app/services/mtime.py, frontend/src/components/search/SearchQueryHeader.tsx, five e2e fixtures, many frontend and mcp-server test files, and (through the shared parser) the intelligence addon's Ask frontend. None of these is in the touch-point list (R1-R5).

Touch points listed but not changed by the diff: frontend/src/lib/api.ts (getDriveFiles and getDriveFilesWithFileIds already route through listingRequest's appendListingFilters, so modified passes through without an edit), FileDetailFullScreen.tsx, SmartFolderSaveButton.tsx, readingAppTarget.ts and VideoAppHeader.tsx. They are reached only as callers of changed functions.
Implicit touch points (docs/specs, INDEX.md, docs/process/reviews) are not reported.

Every other changed product file maps to a listed touch point: models, database, scanner, content_write, upload, fileops, drives, internal, shelves, schemas, markdown_relations, searchQuery, listingRequest, useFolderFiles, useFileSearch, appTarget, videoAppTarget, memberTarget, inNameResolution, searchMerge, FolderTreePane, smartCollectionEval, the route, FileListRow, types, messages, the MCP tools, and the addon file_matching.
potential_unspecified_behavior: os.utime in _ensure_md_id_for_new_file now runs on every new-note registration (scanner pass 2 and register_single_file). Grep shows no other caller, so the reach matches I14.

The search cache (readSearchCache, keyed by query text) can show a relative modified: result computed at an earlier now until revalidation completes. The spec accepts this ('the search cache keys by the query text').
ResolvedModified.hasAbsolute is computed but the route recomputes the absolute check on its own; nothing reads the field.
regression_risks: A change to mtime.py's truncation reaches seven write paths at once, none of which the plan names (R1).
Reordering the entries array in SearchQueryHeader.tsx changes the R-5 first-level layout outside the planned files (R2).
Ask scope parsing in the addon frontend treats modified: as an operator and drops it silently (R5).
